questions.statement: Which sentence uses the third person singular of the verb 'to work' correctly?
questions.context: Present simple third person, San Juan, grado 11, W01.

options.text: She works in a clinic in Carolina.
options.feedback: Correct. 'She works' carries the third-person singular -s, and every other subject in the bundle would drop that ending.

options.text: She work in a clinic in Carolina.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The sentence has a singular subject and a plural-looking verb; this -s is the single most tested point of the unit.

options.text: She working in a clinic in Carolina.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Working' is a present participle and it needs the auxiliary 'is' in a progressive form, which this unit does not use.

options.text: She are working in a clinic in Carolina.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Are working' is the progressive, and 'are' also disagrees with the singular subject 'she', so two rules fail at once.

questions.explanation:
En presente simple la tercera persona singular añade -s al verbo, salvo cuando ya termina en -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -z o -o. Las otras personas no añaden nada. Revisar el sujeto antes que el verbo es el método más seguro para no equivocarse.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'My brother ____ (go) to the plaza every Sunday.'
questions.context: Present simple third person, Caguas, grado 11, W01.

options.feedback: Incorrect. With no ending, the sentence reads as plural; the subject 'my brother' is singular and requires the -es form.
Incorrect. 'Going' is the -ing form, which only appears with the auxiliary 'is' in the present continuous.
Correct. 'Go' ends in -o, so the third-person -s becomes -es to keep it from sounding like 'goose'.
Incorrect. 'Gone' is the past participle, which is used with 'have' and does not describe a weekly routine.

questions.explanation:
La tercera persona singular tiene su propia terminación. Con los verbos terminados en -o el inglés añade -es para que la palabra no termine en -s a secas, igual que ocurre con 'go' y 'does'. El resto de personas no cambia.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which question is formed correctly?
questions.context: Present simple third person, Ponce, grado 11, W01.

options.text: Do your sister live in Ponce?
options.feedback: Incorrect. The auxiliary 'do' has no -s, so it cannot go with a singular subject in a question with a lexical verb.

options.text: Does your sister live in Ponce?
options.feedback: Correct. In questions with 'to be' and with the verb 'to live', the auxiliary 'does' is used, and it already carries the third-person -s.

options.text: Is your sister live in Ponce?
options.feedback: Incorrect. After 'is' you need the participle, not the base form of the verb as it appears in the prompt.

options.text: Your sister does lives in Ponce?
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is not question word order: the auxiliary 'does' must open the sentence before the subject.

questions.explanation:
En presente simple la pregunta con verbos de acción se forma con 'do' o 'does'. Cuando se usa 'does', el verbo principal vuelve a su forma base, porque la -s ya está en el auxiliar. Ese es el error típico: 'does she lives' en lugar de 'does she live'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct negative form: 'He ____ (not / drink) coffee after dinner.'
questions.context: Present simple third person, Bayamon, grado 11, W01.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Don't' is reserved for I, you, we and they; with 'he' the auxiliary must be 'does'.
Incorrect. 'Isn't' forms the negative of the verb 'to be', and the participle does not fit here either.
Incorrect. The auxiliary is missing entirely, and in the present simple the negative is never formed with 'not' alone.
Correct. The negative with 'not' and an action verb is formed with 'does not' or 'doesn't' in the third person singular.

questions.explanation:
El negativo del presente simple tiene dos formas: 'do not / don't' para I, you, we y they, y 'does not / doesn't' para he, she y it. El verbo principal se queda en su forma base detrás del auxiliar, con o sin negación.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which is the correct third person singular form of the verb 'to pass'?
questions.context: Present simple spelling rules, Arecibo, grado 11, W01.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Passs' has three s's and follows no rule; English never doubles the -s in this position.
Incorrect. This is the base form, and the third person singular needs a new ending, even though the final sound is similar.
Incorrect. The -ing form belongs to the present continuous and is not used for a routine in the present simple.
Correct. When the base verb ends in -ss, the third person adds only -es, so the final -s is pronounced correctly.

questions.explanation:
La ortografía de la -s de la tercera persona tiene reglas fijas. Si la base ya acaba en -s, -sh, -ch, -x o -z se añade solo -es. Si acaba en consonante más -o se añade -es. Si termina en -y precedida de consonante, la -y pasa a -ies.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'The committee ____ (try) to finish the project on time.'
questions.context: Present simple spelling rules, Humacao, grado 11, W01.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Adding an -s after a consonant + -y produces a form that no English speaker uses.
Correct. 'Try' ends in -y with a consonant before it, so the -y becomes -ies for the third person singular.
Incorrect. The -y does not turn into a vowel: it changes to -ies, and the verb does not also add an -e.
Incorrect. 'Trying' is the -ing form and belongs to the present continuous, not to a routine in the present simple.

questions.explanation:
Cuando el verbo termina en -y y la consonante anterior no es una vocal, la -y se cambia por -ies: try, tries. Si la -y está precedida de vocal, el verbo es monosilábico y solo añade -s: play, plays. Reconocer la vocal precedente evita el error más común de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the verb 'to have' correctly in the third person singular?
questions.context: Present simple with to have, Carolina, grado 11, W01.

options.text: She has a car in Carolina.
options.feedback: Correct. 'To have' is irregular in the third person: the correct form is 'has', not 'haves' or 'have'.

options.text: She haves a car in Carolina.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Haves' does not exist in English; the irregular -s form of 'to have' replaces the entire base form.

options.text: She have a car in Carolina.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Have' is the base form and is only used with I, you, we and they in the present simple.

options.text: She having a car in Carolina.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The -ing form needs the auxiliary 'is', and 'having' also describes an ongoing action, not habitual possession.

questions.explanation:
El presente simple tiene un puñado de verbos irregulares que no siguen la regla de añadir -s. Los más frecuentes son 'to have', que da 'has', y 'to do', que da 'does'. Estos dos aparecen en casi todos los exámenes de la unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'My parents ____ (live) in Aguadilla.'
questions.context: Present simple with plural subjects, Aguadilla, grado 11, W01.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The -s belongs to the third person singular, and here the subject is plural, so the ending is not needed.
Incorrect. An apostrophe marks possession and is never used to form the present simple of a verb.
Correct. 'My parents' is a plural subject, so the verb stays in its base form with no third-person ending.
Incorrect. 'Lived' is the past simple; the sentence describes a habitual place of residence and calls for the present.

questions.explanation:
La -s de la tercera persona depende del sujeto, no del significado de la frase. Un sujeto plural o plural conceptual como 'my parents', 'people' o 'the team' exige la forma base. El error más común es poner la -s por costumbre y no por análisis del sujeto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which negative question is correct?
questions.context: Present simple negative questions, Guayanilla, grado 11, W01.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Don't' only goes with I, you, we and they; with 'he' the auxiliary has to be 'does'.
Incorrect. 'Isn't' belongs to the verb 'to be', and the main verb would also be left with the wrong -s.
Correct. The auxiliary 'doesn't' opens the question and leaves the main verb in its base form, 'like'.
Incorrect. After 'does' the main verb goes back to its base form, so 'does he not likes' would duplicate the ending and also reverse the order of the tag, which must be auxiliary then pronoun.

questions.explanation:
En las preguntas negativas el orden es siempre el mismo: auxiliar, sujeto y verbo en forma base. Con 'does' el auxiliar ya aporta la -s, asi que escribir el verbo con terminacion duplicaria la marca de tercera persona.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct auxiliary: '____ your teacher speak Spanish during class?'
questions.context: Present simple questions, Trujillo Alto, grado 11, W01.

options.feedback: Correct. The third-person singular auxiliary in the present simple is 'does', and the main verb stays in its base form.
Incorrect. 'Do' is used with I, you, we and they; since the subject is 'your teacher', the -s is missing.
Incorrect. 'Is' forms questions with the verb 'to be', but here the main verb is 'speak'.
Incorrect. 'Are' goes with plural subjects or 'you', and it does not go with a lexical verb like 'speak'.

questions.explanation:
Paraforming preguntas en presente simple hay que mirar primero el sujeto. Si es I, you, we o they se usa 'do'; si es he, she o it se usa 'does'. Solo con el verbo 'to be' aparecen 'am', 'is' y 'are'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'The train ____ (leave) from San Juan at seven every morning.'
questions.context: Present simple with time expressions, Barceloneta, grado 11, W01.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'The train' is singular, so the base form with no ending does not match the subject.
Incorrect. The -ing form belongs to the present continuous, and this routine calls for a present simple verb.
Incorrect. 'Leave' is not a participle, and an action verb also does not combine with 'is' in the present simple.
Correct. 'The train' is third person singular, and since 'leave' already ends in -e, it only adds -s.

questions.explanation:
Cuando el verbo base termina en -e, la tercera persona singular anade unicamente -s, sin -(e)s. Las expresiones de tiempo como 'every morning' o 'always' suelen acompanarse de presente simple, y conviene reconocerlas antes de elegir la forma verbal.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'She ____ (have got) two brothers and one sister.'
questions.context: Present simple with have got, Maunabo, grado 11, W01.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Have got' goes with I, you, we and they; with 'she' you need the form 'has got'.
Correct. In the present simple, the contracted form of 'have got' for the third person singular is 'has got'.
Incorrect. 'Hav' is not a form of the verb 'to have' in English; the participle of that verb is 'had'.
Incorrect. The -ing form describes an ongoing action, not a possession that is permanent.

questions.explanation:
British English usa con frecuencia 'have got' para hablar de posesión, y ese verbo también es irregular en la tercera persona singular. La estructura es 'have got' en el resto de personas y 'has got' con he, she o it.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'He ____ (do) his homework after dinner every day.'
questions.context: Present simple spelling rules, Yauco, grado 11, W01.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Dos' is the number two and not a verb form, so the sentence makes no grammatical sense.
Correct. 'To do' is irregular in the third person: it becomes 'does', and because it is irregular it does not add a regular ending.
Incorrect. 'Do' is the base form and only fits a subject other than he, she or it.
Incorrect. 'Doing' belongs to the present continuous, and a routine is expressed in the present simple.

questions.explanation:
Los verbos irregulares en presente simple se memorizan, no se derivan. 'To do' da 'does', 'to have' da 'has' y 'to go' da 'goes'. Reconocerlos rápido evita construir formas como 'doos' o 'haves'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'Maria ____ (watch) the news at nine every night.'
questions.context: Present simple spelling rules, Cayey, grado 11, W01.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A bare -s after -ch produces an unlikely sound and is not a valid English form.
Incorrect. This is the base form, and the subject 'Maria' is third person singular, so it requires an ending.
Incorrect. 'Watching' is the -ing form and belongs to the present continuous, not to a daily routine.
Correct. Since 'watch' ends in -ch, the third person singular adds -es so that the -s sounds like a normal s.

questions.explanation:
Las reglas ortograficas de la -s de la tercera persona se aprenden como una sola tabla. La clave fonica es que la -s final debe sonar como una s normal, y por eso se escribe -es detras de -ch, -sh, -s, -x y -z.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct negative: 'I ____ (not / like) the rain in San Sebastian.'
questions.context: Present simple negatives with first person, San Sebastian, grado 11, W01.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Doesn't' is third person singular, and here the subject is the first-person 'I'.
Incorrect. 'Am' belongs to the verb 'to be', and the -ing form does not fit an opinion about the weather.
Correct. With 'I' the negative auxiliary is 'do not' or 'don't', and the verb stays in its base form.
Incorrect. The auxiliary is missing: in the present simple the negative is formed with 'do not' or 'does not'.

questions.explanation:
La elección entre 'don't' y 'doesn't' depende únicamente del sujeto. Con I, you, we y they se usa 'don't'; con he, she o it se usa 'doesn't'. En ambos casos el verbo principal permanece en su forma base detrás del auxiliar.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'He ____ (not / be) ready for the exam yet.'
questions.context: Present simple with be in third person, Camuy, grado 11, W01.

options.feedback: Correct. The negative of 'to be' in the third person singular is formed with 'is' plus 'not', or contracted as 'isn't'.
Incorrect. 'Aren't' goes with 'you' or a plural subject, and the subject of the sentence is 'he'.
Incorrect. 'Doesn't' is the auxiliary for action verbs, but here the main verb is 'to be'.
Incorrect. 'Don't' does not combine with 'to be', because the verb 'to be' has its own set of forms.

questions.explanation:
El presente simple de 'to be' es un sistema aparte: I am, you are, he, she e it is, y nosotros, ustedes y ellos son 'are'. El negativo se forma con 'not' detrás del verbo. Los auxiliares 'do' y 'does' nunca participan con 'to be'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct question tag: 'Your cousin lives in Caguas, ____?'
questions.context: Present simple question tags, Luquillo, grado 11, W01.

options.feedback: Correct. A positive statement calls for a negative tag, and since the subject is third person, the tag uses 'doesn't' plus the pronoun.
Incorrect. 'Isn't' belongs to the verb 'to be', and the statement contains no form of 'to be'.
Incorrect. 'Don't' does not go with a third-person singular subject, so the tag is grammatically impossible.
Incorrect. The tag repeats the structure of the statement, but the correct order is auxiliary then pronoun.

questions.explanation:
Las reglas ortograficas de la -s de la tercera persona se aprenden como una sola tabla. La clave fonica es que la -s final debe pronunciarse de manera clara, y por eso se escribe -es detras de -ch, -sh, -s, -x y -z.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'Every student ____ (need) a notebook for the course.'
questions.context: Present simple with quantifiers, Toa Baja, grado 11, W01.

options.feedback: Incorrect. In English, a subject with 'every' requires a singular verb, even if the noun that goes with it is plural.
Incorrect. 'Needing' is an -ing form and belongs to the present continuous, not to a general fact about the course.
Incorrect. The verb 'to need' does not take 'are' in front of it, and the subject of the sentence is also singular.
Correct. 'Every student' is singular in English, so the verb takes the third-person singular form.

questions.explanation:
En ingles los cuantificadores como 'every', 'each' y 'either' governs el verbo en singular. La concordancia se hace con el cuantificador y no con el sustantivo, por lo que 'every student needs' es la estructura correcta.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'The committee ____ (meet) on Mondays to plan the fair.'
questions.context: Present simple with collective nouns, Naguabo, grado 11, W01.

options.feedback: Incorrect. If the committee were treated as several members, the form would be 'meet', but here the group acts as a single entity.
Correct. A group with a single function is treated as a singular unit in English, so the verb is 'meets'.
Incorrect. 'Meeting' is the -ing form and also a noun, so it cannot fill the verb slot.
Incorrect. The apostrophe is not used to form the present simple, and the sentence calls for a present verb form.

questions.explanation:
Los sustantivos colectivos como 'committee', 'team' o 'family' pueden concordar en singular o en plural segun el contexto. Cuando el grupo actua como una unidad con una sola funcion, el verbo va en singular; cuando se habla de cada miembro por separado, va en plural.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the tag that completes the question: 'He ____ he forget the keys?'
questions.context: Present simple tag questions, Hatillo, grado 11, W01.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Don't' belongs to I, you, we and they, and the subject of the main clause is 'he'.
Incorrect. 'Isn't' is the auxiliary for the verb 'to be', and the question is built with 'forget'.
Correct. A negative question calls for a positive tag, and with 'he' that auxiliary is 'does', in the contracted form 'doesn't'.
Incorrect. 'Hasn't' belongs to the present perfect with 'have', not to a present simple question.

questions.explanation:
El tag confirma o matiza lo que dice la frase principal. Si la frase es negativa el tag es positivo, y si es positiva el tag es negativo. En presente simple el auxiliar disponible para 'he' es 'does', y el verbo principal queda en forma base.
